name: Up the Strip
description: Note that the memory limit in this problem is lower than in others. You have a vertical strip with $$$n$$$ cells, numbered consecutively from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ from top to bottom. You also have a token that is initially placed in cell $$$n$$$. You will move the token up until it arrives at cell $$$1$$$. Let the token be in cell $$$x \gt 1$$$ at some moment. One shift of the token can have either of the following kinds: Subtraction: you choose an integer $$$y$$$ between $$$1$$$ and $$$x-1$$$, inclusive, and move the token from cell $$$x$$$ to cell $$$x - y$$$. Floored division: you choose an integer $$$z$$$ between $$$2$$$ and $$$x$$$, inclusive, and move the token from cell $$$x$$$ to cell $$$\lfloor \frac{x}{z} \rfloor$$$ ($$$x$$$ divided by $$$z$$$ rounded down). Find the number of ways to move the token from cell $$$n$$$ to cell $$$1$$$ using one or more shifts, and print it modulo $$$m$$$. Note that if there are several ways to move the token from one cell to another in one shift, all these ways are considered distinct (check example explanation for a better understanding).
input_specification: The only line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 4 \cdot 10^6$$$; $$$10^8 \lt m \lt 10^9$$$; $$$m$$$ is a prime number) — the length of the strip and the modulo.
output_specification: Print the number of ways to move the token from cell $$$n$$$ to cell $$$1$$$, modulo $$$m$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
